SRC-ZHOU-2021.summary: Study of 234 Taiwanese SMEs reports nonlinear effects of exploration and exploitation and a positive interaction involving ambidexterity and market orientation.

SRC-CLAUSS-2021.summary: Mixed-method study of 150 German mid-sized firms reports that ambidexterity did not uniformly improve competitive advantage and could have a negative association without strategic fit.

SRC-WAHAB-2024.summary: Cross-sectional study of 417 Lebanese SMEs tests AI assimilation, absorptive capacity, customer agility, organizational agility and firm performance, supporting mediated and moderated associations.

SRC-SANCHEZ-2025.locator: Abstract; Theoretical Framework; Research Instrument; Results; Limitations
SRC-SANCHEZ-2025.summary: Open-access study of 385 Ecuadorian SMEs reports uneven AI adoption, barriers in skills, data and finance, and associations between adoption, dynamic capabilities and strategic innovation performance.

source_conflicts.claim_scope: Effect of organizational ambidexterity on performance and competitive advantage
source_conflicts.context_difference: The studies use different countries, firm populations, constructs, outcomes and operationalizations; one emphasizes SME performance and market orientation, while the other examines competitive advantage and strategic agility in German mid-sized firms.
source_conflicts.resolution: Treat ambidexterity as a contingent and potentially nonlinear architecture. Require tests of curvature, strategic agility and resource constraints rather than a universal positive hypothesis.

source_conflicts.claim_scope: Whether AI assimilation or adoption causes superior SME performance
source_conflicts.context_difference: The AI studies report cross-sectional associations and mediation models in Lebanon and Ecuador, whereas the ambidexterity study shows that simultaneous strategic orientations can reduce competitive advantage under coordination costs.
source_conflicts.resolution: Frame AI-performance relationships as provisional associations mediated by organizational capabilities. Do not claim causality without temporal or quasi-experimental evidence.
